root_cause.text: The authencesn module lacks a minimum length check for the AAD (assoclen), allowing a too-short input (less than 8 bytes) to cause out-of-bounds scatterlist access and a NULL pointer dereference when the code assumes an ESP/ESN-formatted AAD.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks `if (assoclen < 8) return -EINVAL;` in both `crypto_authenc_esn_encrypt()` and `crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt()`. The CVE description and commit message state that with assoclen < 8, the decrypt function can advance past the end of the destination scatterlist, triggering a NULL pointer dereference in `scatterwalk_map_and_copy()`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The functions crypto_authenc_esn_genicv (lines 280-320) and crypto_authenc_esn_iverify (lines 400-440) parse the associated data scatterlist but only verify that there are at least three scatterlist entries via sg_is_last checks. This missing minimum length check leaves the code vulnerable to out-of-bounds scatterlist access and NULL pointer dereference when too-short AAD is supplied. The commit introduces this code without any such check, so the bug is present and not fixed.
